title: Post-incident: Gateway rate limiter regression causing client 429 surge for long-lived streams
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: On 2026-02-28 we observed a sudden spike in 429 responses from the API gateway affecting a subset of customers using long-lived streaming connections (primarily websocket/proxied HTTP streams). The surge coincided with gateway-2.14.0 deployment which included a refactor of token parsing and rate-limit key generation. Impact: several customers experienced repeated throttling leading to degraded product functionality and increased token refresh attempts, which amplified load and led to transient backend saturation. Root cause: a regression in the rate-limiter key normalization logic introduced in gateway-2.14.0. The refactor changed how client identity was derived: when X-Forwarded-For was present and a bearer token had a rotation suffix, the normalization produced non-deterministic keys for the same client session. This caused the limiter to treat many related requests as separate clients hitting a shared global threshold, triggering aggressive enforcement. Secondary contributing factors: lack of unit tests around token suffix normalization, insufficient canary coverage for long-lived streams, and alerts tuned for aggregate 5xx rather than 429 noise. Mitigation: we rolled back gateway-2.14.0 at 02:18 UTC, released hotfix gateway-2.14.1 with corrected normalization by 04:00 UTC, and applied temporary rate-limit easing for affected customer orgs until the fix was rolled out. We also deployed a dashboard to track 429 rate by org and stream-bearing sessions. Next steps and action items enumerated below.
timeline: 2026-02-28 01:05 UTC: Pager triggered for elevated 4xx rates on api-gateway service (on-call: Luis).
2026-02-28 01:20 UTC: Initial triage identified sharp increase in 429s concentrated on streaming endpoints; correlated with release history showing gateway-2.14.0 at 00:50 UTC.
2026-02-28 01:45 UTC: Rollback decision made after canary showed identical spike; rollback executed at 02:18 UTC.
2026-02-28 03:30 UTC: Hotfix branch created; patch to normalization logic and additional tests landed (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/4120).
2026-02-28 04:00 UTC: Hotfix deployed as gateway-2.14.1 to all regions; affected customers reported reduction in 429s.
2026-02-28 06:00 UTC: Temporary rate-limit easing policy applied to 8 orgs via emergency config toggle to reduce customer impact while rollback/hotfix propagated.
2026-03-01 10:30 UTC: Post-incident meeting: confirmed root cause, action items, and owner assignments.
2026-03-05 15:00 UTC: Draft postmortem written; PR opened for playbook updates and observability improvements.
action_items: AG-1: Add deterministic token normalization unit tests covering X-Forwarded-For and rotated token suffix cases (owner: Priya Nair, estimate: 3d, due: 2026-03-10)
AG-2: Add an integration test that simulates long-lived streams with token rotation to CI canaries (owner: Luis Ortega, estimate: 5d, due: 2026-03-19)
AG-3: Implement 429-by-org dashboard and alert with SLO-based burn-rate signal (owner: R&D Observability team lead - Jonas, estimate: 3d, due: 2026-03-08)

AG-4: Update deployment gating to include canary traffic patterns for streaming endpoints and require 30m of canary stability under production payload (owner: Release Engineering, estimate: 2d, due: 2026-03-15)
AG-5: Create post-incident runbook entry for rate-limit regressions covering rollback, emergency easing, and communication templates (owner: Maya Chen, estimate: 1d, due: 2026-03-05)
AG-6: Perform targeted chaos testing on rate-limiter key generation logic in staging (owner: SRE, estimate: 4d, due: 2026-03-22)
AG-7: Customer outreach: coordinate with CSMs to send incident summaries and compensatory credits where affected orgs request them (owner: Customer Success, estimate: 1d, due: 2026-03-07)
AG-8: Add regression test to ensure global threshold semantics unchanged when clients present equivalent session identifiers (owner: Testing, estimate: 2d, due: 2026-03-12)
AG-9: Audit other recent refactors touching identity normalization; flag risky PRs for additional review (owner: Security/Code Review Board, estimate: 2d, due: 2026-03-11)
notes: We observed token refresh storms from some client SDK implementations that aggressively retried on 429; recommend SDK rate-limit backoff guidance update.
Canary policy gap: streaming endpoints have much longer-lived sessions than typical HTTP paths; future release gates must account for sustained open connections.
Consider adding a deterministic fallback identity (session-id header) that client SDKs can opt into to reduce reliance on heuristics for rate-limiter keys.
